title: 'St. Louis Blues' and Basie dealing with advisers
summary: Stanley Dance recalls Basie calling an arrangement a satire to Teddy Reig; Greene says he doesn't interfere.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Do you remember that arrangement the band was playing about seven or eight years ago -- 'St. Louis Blues' It was a long thing. I think it was a head or maybe Thad had something to do with it. But, you know --
-- Lockjaw played and then built up with the trumpets.

They recorded that -- well, you recorded that. And, I always remember I was standing in there -- in the studio -- and Basie comes through with Teddy Reig. And, Teddy had evidently been saying it was old fashioned, or something like that, you know. And, Basie was saying -- 'well, look at it as a kind of satire'. (laugh).
And, it was ridiculous. It was the best thing they recorded --.
And, he was having to persuade Teddy Reig that it was a kind of satire on music you know. You don't know what a guy like Basie has to go through with, you know.
Well, Freddie, to me -- you're the one guy that does know. I see it -- you know, the different times that I've come around
I see things happening -- and I see you seeing
And, Basie having it a certain way, and -- I mean -- you're always aware of it.
Nobody knows better than you do how Basie handles things.
Well, you see I've been there a long time, and whatever way he handles it, that's -- you know.
That's him. You know. I don't interfere (laugh).
No. I mean I figure half the time you're smiling to yourself, because you can see how he is handling it, you know.
Yeah. Yeah. No, I wouldn't question about the way he handled it, you know.
No. Well, it's far from easy.
I mean, he may make it look easy.
But, it's not easy, is it? I mean things that 2 band leaders impinge on our like that -- alot of times are a drag.
